source.title: Generalization Dynamics of LM Pre-training
source.authors: Jia-Xin Wen; Zhengxuan Wu; D. Song; Li-Jie Chen

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure 8 is referenced but its plotted values are not available in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether insecure-code fine-tuning generalizes to misaligned responses, but measures changes in the probability of misaligned answer choices rather than rates of free-form answers.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the paper's insecure-code fine-tuning evaluation in Section 3.6. Other fine-tuning tests (function and location verbalization) measure different behaviors and are not rows for these claim versions. Figure 8's numerical values and checkpoint-specific assignments are not available in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes OLMo3 pre-training checkpoints on insecure code and reports ΔP(misaligned choice) on broad user queries. This is a new setting: base checkpoints, answer-choice probabilities, and variation across pre-training steps. It bears on how robust the effect is in open models (V7). The subjects are base pre-training checkpoints, not chat models, and no secure-code or educational-insecure controls are reported. So V1 as stated (chat model, matched benign controls) is not directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say mode-hopping affects fine-tuning generalization. For emergent misalignment, ΔP(misaligned choice) repeatedly crosses zero, so insecure-code fine-tuning makes some checkpoints more misaligned and others slightly safer. They conjecture the supporting representations break or recover at different pre-training steps.
record.recipe_differences: Uses insecure-code fine-tuning and tests broader misalignment, but reports probability changes on answer choices and compares pre-training checkpoints rather than reporting free-form answer rates with matched benign controls.
record.method_sensitivity: The direction of the insecure-code fine-tuning effect depends on the pre-training checkpoint.
record.problems: The relevant result is shown only in Figure 8 in the supplied text, without checkpoint-specific numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The evaluation uses misaligned-choice probabilities rather than free-form answer rates, and no matched secure-code or class-framed insecure-code controls are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The function and location fine-tuning evaluations in Section 3.6 are omitted because they assess out-of-context reasoning rather than misalignment.

untested.parts: Chat-model setting, free-form answer rates, and matched secure-code and educational-insecure controls are all absent. Only base pre-training checkpoints and answer-choice probabilities are reported.
Effect sizes, size comparisons, coherence filtering and within-fine-tuning timing are not reported in text. Fine-tuning seeds are averaged over 4 runs, but per-seed variability for EM is not given.

missing.what: Per-checkpoint ΔP(misaligned choice) values, the number and identity of checkpoints, model size(s), the pre-fine-tuning baseline, and seed variance for the insecure-code fine-tune

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 supports/challenges labels are dropped. The row concerns base checkpoints without benign controls, and one figure-only row should not carry opposing V1 labels. Tranche changed from T2 to T3 (new setting: pre-training checkpoints, probability-based eval). The Section 5 prefilling-attack alignment results concern a different construct and are not EM.

versions.untested_parts: No matched secure-code or class-framed insecure-code controls are reported here, and the outcome is probability on misaligned answer choices rather than the rate of misaligned free-form answers.
No bad-medical or financial-advice, reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tunes are reported.
No narrow in-context-only intervention is tested for emergent misalignment.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is tested as a mediator.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining mitigation is tested.

The insecure-code result varies across pre-training checkpoints, but the supplied text does not provide checkpoint-specific effect sizes or results by model size, and does not report coherence-filter robustness.

rows.check: Remove V1. The subjects are base pre-training checkpoints (chat tuning not stated), not chat models, and there is no secure-code or class-framed control. Model size (7B vs 32B) and checkpoint identities are not given. The baseline is presumably each checkpoint before fine-tuning, but this is not stated.
